findings.title: Denial cache is consulted before permissions, so a cached denial defeats the fix for newly created resources
findings.body: Check now returns a cached denial (keyed by user, action, name and parent folder) before looking at permissions. The denial is written at line ~153 whenever a check is denied and lives for shortCacheTTL (30s). The PR's stated goal is that a creator can access a dashboard or folder they just created. If the creator (or anyone) is checked for that name before it exists, the denial is cached. Once the resource is created and the user gets access, the next Check still hits the denial cache and returns Allowed=false for up to 30s. The new 'requery from DB on cache miss' logic never runs in that window. Name-less checks (create verbs, where Name is empty) are cached the same way, so a denied create can block a subsequent allowed create for 30s. Denials should not be cached for resources that may be created, or the denial cache should be invalidated when permissions change.

findings.title: Negative results are cached for every denied check, including name-less checks
findings.body: The denial entry is set for every denied request, with no regard for whether the target exists yet or whether Name is empty. For verbs like create (Name empty), checkPermission returns len(scopeMap)>0, so a user with no permissions is denied and that denial is cached under a key with an empty name. Any later create within 30s is denied from cache even after the user is granted permissions. Caching negatives this broadly also means permission revocations are not reflected for the TTL of the denial, which is not documented.

findings.title: Denial cache key concatenates unescaped fields, so distinct requests can collide
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins userUID, action, name and parent with '_' and no escaping. Names and folder UIDs can contain underscores, so (name='a_b', parent='') and (name='a', parent='b') produce the same key. A denial for one resource would then be applied to another. The key also shares the '.perm_' prefix with userPermCacheKey, so it can collide with permission-cache entries if identifiers contain '_'. A separator that cannot appear in these fields, or a hash of the tuple, is needed.

findings.title: No test covers the actual regression: denial then creation then allow
findings.body: TestService_CacheCheck covers an explicit denial entry, a cache miss, and an outdated cache, but none checks the scenario this PR targets. A user is denied for a resource, the resource is then created and the permission granted, and the next Check must allow. The 'explicit deny' test seeds the denial cache by hand and only checks that denial wins. Without a test for the denial-then-grant sequence, the bug above goes unnoticed. The removed getUserPermissions cache-hit case also leaves no test that exercises the cache path through getIdentityPermissions.
